clue.text: He's not assertive enough with a naughty child

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous, naughty child

explanation.surface: A parent who lacks the backbone to discipline a badly behaved child.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, timid person who never stands up for himself is a weakling, which is the slang sense.

clue.text: For instance, fighter's bitterness when on the road

annotationWithheld.why: For instance, fighter's bitterness when on the road (8): WARPLANE is defined by 'For instance, fighter' and LANE is 'road', but no sense of 'bitterness' gives WARP, and no other parse was found
annotationWithheld.clue: For instance, fighter's bitterness when on the road

clue.text: Think referee has overrun time

indicators.note: has overrun means the word for referee spreads over and around the other piece

parts.note: to mediate is to act as referee in a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone reckons the match official let the game run on too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'referee' looks like a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or contemplate deeply is to think.

clue.text: Staff in a line to shut up things in shop

parts.note: to pen animals is to shut them up in an enclosure
a shop's stock is the goods it holds for sale

explanation.surface: A member of shop staff told to keep the merchandise locked away in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like shop employees, but it is a walking pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A long iron-tipped walking pole used by climbers in the Alps is a kind of staff.

clue.text: Drinking establishment a company set up in the fifties

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A pub opened by a firm back in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns A CO into OCA, which goes between the two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the pub nearest your home is your neighbourhood watering hole.

clue.text: My one opus turned out like Hamlet

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters have been rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A writer finds a single great work has come out resembling Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the title character of his play, so the work is named after him.

clue.text: City where foreign money is put into dodgy casinos

indicators.note: put into means one piece is placed inside the other
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and is still used in Switzerland

explanation.surface: A place where foreign cash is laundered through shady gambling houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' is the anagram signal and 'put into' the container: the foreign money sits inside the rearranged gambling houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian port on its famous bay is a major US city.

clue.text: Tree house

definitions.meaning: a citrus tree bearing round fruit
a European royal dynasty, as in William of the Dutch line

explanation.definitionFit: It names a fruit tree and also the Dutch royal dynasty, house in the sense of family line.

clue.text: Rig up trap for little animal

parts.note: rig and kit both mean an outfit of gear

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: Set a snare to catch a small creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is a small animal.

clue.text: Controlled the way we speak

indicators.note: what we speak is said out loud, so a word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a road is a way to travel along

explanation.surface: Someone governed the manner of our speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ridden a horse is to have controlled and steered it.

clue.text: Description given by worker for auditor

parts.note: an account is a description or report of events
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A job reference written by an employee for a financial inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is a professional who examines books of figures, the work of a qualified bookkeeper.

clue.text: Composer providing actor/manager with capital

parts.note: Sir Henry Irving was a famous Victorian actor-manager
Berlin is the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: A musician who gives a theatre impresario some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote White Christmas and many Broadway songs, an American songwriter.

clue.text: Measure of drink for American friend? Exactly!

parts.note: the metric measure of a litre is spelt liter in American usage
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone checks that a US pal really gets a standard measure of drink, and is told yes, precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an exclamation, the word agrees emphatically, meaning precisely or to the letter.

clue.text: Scoundrel and libertine, but good at heart

indicators.note: at heart means placed in the middle of the word for libertine

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a libertine

explanation.surface: A villain and rake who nonetheless has a kind nature deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or knave is a dishonest, unprincipled person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: No fear of being unemployed? Just the reverse

indicators.note: just the reverse tells us to swap the order of the two words in the phrase for being unemployed

parts.note: someone unemployed is idle, without work to do

explanation.surface: A jobless person apparently has no worries about being out of work, or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Being unemployed is DOING NOTHING; 'Just the reverse' swaps its two words round. 'No fear' is a definition, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal refusals, emphatic ways of saying certainly not.

clue.text: Mark in red metallic element

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: geranium is a shade of bright red, named after the flower

explanation.surface: A correction marked in red ink on a chemistry paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a plain colour, but the setter means geranium, the flower's red shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Element 32 is a grey semimetal used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Reserved novel — it's held up

indicators.note: held means one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: novel and recent both mean new

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the 's here is a link, is, so only the word it gives letters

explanation.surface: A new book is delayed, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but means new.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved is restrained and slow to reveal thoughts or feelings.

clue.text: Wild frenzy and disorder this year

indicators.note: disorder means the letters are thrown into a jumbled arrangement

explanation.surface: Twelve months of chaos and wild excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrolled emotional excitement is a wild frenzy.

clue.text: Silver-grey vessel I have left concealed, with hostile intent

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: concealed means the other pieces are hidden inside the word for grey

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship, a vessel
I have contracts to I've, giving these letters without the I

explanation.surface: A silvery-grey warship slipped out of sight, ready to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have' contracts to I've, so it supplies three letters, not just I. 'Silver-grey' looks like one colour but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting belligerently means behaving in an attacking, hostile manner.

clue.text: Modest constant speed

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
haste means speed

explanation.surface: A steady pace that is unassuming.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest in the sense of pure and virtuous, especially sexually restrained.

clue.text: Entrance with precious metal and rich food

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A doorway decorated with gold leads to a lavish feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich cream cake is a luxurious food.

clue.text: Cast get over closure of theatre

indicators.note: over here means one word goes round the other, covering it

parts.note: to have something is to get or obtain it

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Actors in a play try to get past the news that the theatre is shutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a set of actors, but it is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave a heavy object is to throw or hurl it, as to cast it.

clue.text: Revolutionary's attempt to impose silence on a government agent

definitions.note: the definition reads revolutionary is, so the answer is a noun naming such a person

indicators.note: on means the call for silence is placed after, as if added onto, the agent piece

parts.note: a narc is an American narcotics agent working for the government
hist is an old exclamation calling for silence

explanation.surface: A rebel tries to shut up an official who is investigating him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary's' reads as a possessive but means revolutionary is. NARC is US slang for a drugs agent, and hist! is an old call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wants to overthrow all government and authority is a revolutionary.

clue.text: Check uranium found in entrance to mine

indicators.note: found in means one piece is located inside another

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An inspector looks for uranium at a mine's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An official examination of accounts is a check.

clue.text: Spend bills in exchange for charms

indicators.note: in exchange suggests letters being traded around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spending money on bills in return for lucky trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charms' looks like a noun (trinkets) but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to hold them under a magic spell, as a captivator does.

clue.text: Drop in speed

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye when crying
to rush along at great speed

explanation.definitionFit: A drop from a weeping eye is one sense; dashing headlong is the other, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Composure displayed by mimic taken back into theatrical group

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union

indicators.note: taken back means the word for mimic is read backwards

parts.note: the mina, or mynah, is a bird famed for mimicking speech

explanation.surface: Calmness shown by an impressionist who rejoined a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns the mimic round and 'into' places it inside the actors' union. The mina, also spelt mynah, is a talking bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmness of mind, especially under pressure, is a synonym for composure.

clue.text: Greeks' walk from Piraeus to Athens

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Greek people's walk from the port of Piraeus up to Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered colonnade where ancient Greeks would walk and talk is a portico.
